title: Network toxicology and molecular docking identify candidate molecular links between bis (1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
content:
by Zihui Liu, Huanfang Fan, Dehui Li, Yun He, Jiatong Yin, Yiting Gu

Bis(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate (BDCIPP), a major metabolite and urinary biomarker of tris(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TDCIPP), has recently been associated with an increased risk of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC); however, the molecular basis of this association remains poorly understood. This study integrated in silico toxicity profiling, network toxicology, functional enrichment analysis, and molecular docking to investigate the potential molecular links between BDCIPP and ESCC. BDCIPP-related targets were collected from TargetNet, SwissTargetPrediction, STITCH, and CTD, whereas ESCC-related targets were obtained from GeneCards, OMIM, and TTD. Intersecting the two target sets yielded 102 common targets, and protein–protein interaction (PPI) network analysis prioritized 10 candidate hub targets, including EGFR, CASP3, CTNNB1, MYC, ESR1, MMP9, SRC, PTGS2, ERBB2, and SIRT1. Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis highlighted apoptosis-related regulation and extracellular matrix disassembly, whereas Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis revealed enrichment of cancer-related pathways, including ErbB, PI3K–Akt, MAPK, and focal adhesion, as well as inflammatory and chemical carcinogenesis-related pathways. Molecular docking indicated varying degrees of predicted structural compatibility between BDCIPP and the candidate hub proteins, with ERBB2 exhibiting the lowest top-ranked MOE docking score among the examined proteins. Cross-method integration further highlighted EGFR/ERBB2-centered signaling, MMP9-associated extracellular matrix remodeling, PTGS2-related inflammatory regulation, and CASP3/SIRT1-mediated apoptotic control as candidate mechanistic modules. By focusing specifically on BDCIPP rather than extrapolating mechanistic evidence from its parent compound TDCIPP, these findings delineate a systems-level molecular framework potentially linking BDCIPP to ESCC and provide prioritized, experimentally testable targets and pathways for subsequent exposure-informed validation.
